subject: Hybrid HIPAA + Residency: capex credits, auditlog tiers, HSM seat vs usage
messages:
From: Mark Feldman <mark.feldman@novaturf.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novaturf.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: HIPAA + EU residency + cost model questions

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the demo last week. We like Redwood's latency and the audit-log granularity, but procurement needs clarity on how you price the compliance pieces for an enterprise pilot:

- Audit logs: retention tiers (30 / 90 / 365) and how those are billed (per GB / tiered flat fee).
- KMS/HSM: can you do a model with an up-front capex (reserved HSM seats) vs pure opex (per-request HSM ops)? We need to assess our capital approvals.
- Data residency: we require EU residency for PHI for certain cohorts — can you confirm region isolation and any surcharge?
- HIPAA BAA: timeline for sign and whether any additional implementation fee is typical.

Procurement attached a sheet with our baseline questions (see Novaturf_Procurement_Qs.xlsx). Can you put together an example pricing sketch (pilot-level: 5M tokens/month, audit logs 90d) and call out where credits or one-time implementation fees apply?

Appreciate it — can we have a reply by EOD Tuesday?

Best,
Mark
Chief Security Officer
Novaturf Health
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Mark Feldman <mark.feldman@novaturf.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novaturf.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: HIPAA + EU residency + cost model questions

Hi Mark —

Thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Quick answers up front, then I pulled in Laura (Acct Exec) and will loop Finance for the capex/credit ask:

- Audit logs: we support the three retention tiers you listed. Pricing model options: per-GB ingestion + storage (default), or a blended tiered flat for predictable budgets. For a 5M token pilot we can show both line-item per-GB and a pilot flat that caps cost at X (see proposed sketch I'll email Wednesday).
- KMS/HSM: we offer (a) HSM seats (reserved, one-time provisioning + annual seat fee) that look like capex from a customer's standpoint, or (b) per-request HSM (opx) billed by request volume. We can model a hybrid: 1 reserved seat + per-request overflow.
- Residency: EU region isolation is available (eu-west-1). We enforce network and key separation for customers with residency requirements. There is typically a residency surcharge to cover dedicated tenancy/orchestration — we can show a 1.15x surcharge vs hosted for the pilot.
- BAA: we can sign BAAs within 2 business weeks; implementation work (SOW) is usually a one-time professional services fee if you require custom onboarding.

Laura — can you help with the pilot pricing sketch and whether Sales can offer an onboarding credit for implementation (CapEx-sensitive customers often ask for a one-time credit against MRR for the first N months)?

Mark — I'll consolidate and send a worked example Wednesday EOD. If you can highlight which cohorts need EU residency vs US, that will help sizing.

Cheers,
Sofia
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement <procure@novaturf.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: HIPAA + EU residency + cost model questions

Sofia / Laura —

Thanks. A few clarifications from our side (attached). Highlights:

- We prefer a capex path for HSM (raises fewer monthly approvals) but need to avoid a large one-time capital request. If you can show an amortized credit (apply X% of seat cost back over 12 months) that's compelling.
- Audit logs: procurement wants a flat predictable line for pilots (not per-GB volatility). If Redwood offers a 90-day pilot-flat option that rolls into per-GB after pilot with a 30-day notice, that would work.
- Residency surcharge: can you provide a range (e.g., 10–25%) rather than a single number — our finance will pick based on contract length.

Attached: Novaturf_Procurement_Qs.xlsx with highlighted rows. Also, if you have a sample SOW for BAA onboarding and a short invoiceable list (implementation items + estimated hours), please include.

Procurement (on behalf of Novaturf)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Mark Feldman <mark.feldman@novaturf.com>, Procurement <procure@novaturf.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: HIPAA + EU residency + cost model questions

Mark / Procurement —

Attached are two items: (1) a worked pricing sketch for the 5M-token pilot (see attachment stub: Novaturf_SOW_requirements.pdf contains the SOW + itemized implementation fees), and (2) an example commercial structure we can put on the table while legal/finance finalize terms. Quick summary below.

Summary proposal (pilot: 5M tokens/month, audit logs 90d, EU residency for specified cohorts):

- Audit logs: Pilot-flat: $3,500/month (ingest + 90d retention capped). Post-pilot: per-GB at $0.12/GB with 30d notice.
- HSM: Option A (CapEx-like) — 1 reserved HSM seat: one-time provisioning $18,000 + annual seat fee $4,000. Offer: amortized credit = 50% of provisioning fee applied over first 12 months (reduces net capex impact). Option B (OpEx) — per-request HSM ops at $0.0008/op (overflow only). Hybrid available.
- Residency surcharge: tiered scale based on commitment length — 12mo: 20% surcharge; 24mo: 15%; 36mo+: 10%. We can tighten to a firm number once contract length is set.
- BAA & Onboarding: BAA signature within 10 business days pending standard reviews. Implementation SOW (estimated 40–80 hrs) billed as one-time fee; Sales can offer a $6,000 onboarding credit for pilots converting to committed annual contracts within 90 days.

Logan — finance confirmed the amortized-credit construct is doable; I copied him for any calendar/PO/invoice constraints. Laura — if this looks reasonable for a commercial counter, can you confirm and I’ll send a single-sheet proposal for Mark to review?

Next steps:
- Mark: confirm which user cohorts require EU region isolation (list by dataset / environment).
- Procurement: accept pilot-flat approach vs per-GB and confirm whether the amortized credit helps avoid a capital approval.
- Redwood: deliver single-sheet with options A/B and a sample SOW by Friday.

Thanks —
Sofia
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
